title: control/ is a deterministic state machine; no LLM call belongs there
body: The control plane forks VMs, dispatches agents, and reconciles run state over Postgres/SQLite rows. All intelligence lives inside the forked VM, in the agent. control/README.md states this explicitly as an architectural invariant: 'If a model call ever appears in this repo, something has gone wrong architecturally.' When extending control/, prefer state-machine transitions on the `runs` table over adding judgment calls.

title: control and telemetry share one SQLite file but own separate tables and connection helpers
body: control/db.py and telemetry/store.py both point at the same `var/factory.db` (control/config.py:166, telemetry/config.py:20), but each defines its own connect()/init() over aiosqlite and its own tables, with idempotent init() called on boot so there is no separate migration step. telemetry never imports control.db, and control never reads a telemetry table (telemetry/store.py's module docstring); the two communicate only through that shared database file and run_id. Dependency direction is one-way — control imports telemetry, never the reverse (telemetry/README.md "Dependency direction is one-way").

title: telemetry/normalize.py isolates all runtime-specific event vocabulary behind an adapter
body: ClaudeCodeAdapter (and the ADAPTERS registry) in telemetry/normalize.py is the one place that knows what a given agent runtime's events look like; no table in the repo mentions Claude by name. Adding a second coding agent means writing a new adapter against events recorded from a real run, not changing callers. An unrecognized `events` string in the golden manifest falls back to NullAdapter (empty results, no exception) rather than failing the run.

title: Fast verification is ruff --select F,E9 plus plain __main__ test modules, nothing else
body: CI's only two gates: `.venv/bin/ruff check --select F,E9 control telemetry` (full `ruff check` is red on arrival by design and is not the gate — it reports pre-existing style debt out of scope for any single issue), and running every `control/*_test.py` / `telemetry/*_test.py` as `python -m <module>`. There is no pytest and no test runner; a test registers itself by existing at that path with a `__main__` block, following the shape of the file beside it (verified: both commands pass clean on main@68923d9).

title: Control plane runs on a Hetzner VM under systemd, not on boxd itself
body: The control plane moved off boxd on 2026-08-19 after the box it ran on had its root filesystem corrupt, taking run history with it: the thing the factory forks VMs *from* should not also be the thing that remembers what it did. Deploy is `scripts/deploy.sh` (pulls tracked branch, rebuilds, restarts `factory.service`); TLS is Caddy, not boxd's proxy; secrets live only in `.env` on the box. boxd is still where every run VM comes from — the Hetzner box only talks to it over the API (BOXD_API_KEY).

title: One GitHub credential serves the control plane and every run VM, and it needs repo + workflow
body: control/config.py resolves GITHUB_TOKEN (env first, then `gh auth token`) and runner.dispatch_env hands that same value to every run VM as GH_TOKEN. So one credential covers both the control plane's API calls — labels, run comments, the auto-merge — and everything the agent does inside the VM: clone, push, `gh pr create`. It has to carry `repo` and `workflow`. Without `workflow`, GitHub rejects the whole push the moment any commit in it touches .github/workflows/*, even when every other file in the push is fine; that is what mem_0d3c recorded, and the credential in use since 2026-08-20 has the scope, so workflow files are editable again. Without write access to contents it is worse: the run clones, spends its whole context, and dies at the push — or opens a pull request the auto-merge then cannot land, refused with a bare 403.

title: Goldens are named for the repo, not the agent; the base is golden-copy
body: agents.resolve_snapshot (control/agents.py) picks `golden-<owner-repo>` (the warm tier, repo pre-cloned) if it exists, else `golden-copy` (the base image: tooling and agent auth, no repo), else nothing. The agent is deliberately absent from the name — which agent an image launches is what the image announces in /etc/factory/agent.json, read off the FACTORY-MANIFEST line and written to runs.agent in control/runner.py. Nothing derives an agent from a snapshot name any more, and there is no FACTORY_AGENT_DEFAULT. The two tiers matter because the fallback is what makes connecting a repo cheap: an unprovisioned repo is not an error, it boots the base and installs for itself — step 2 of the run prompt is "Install this project's dependencies, before you touch any code", and the prompt says plainly that "nothing is installed for this repo yet". scripts/refresh-golden.sh says it from the other side: "A warm golden is a speed-up; every run installs for itself". So a missing warm snapshot costs minutes, not correctness, and provisioning may finish after the first run has already gone out.

title: Watched repos are a DB register with a sync cache; nothing about a golden gates dispatch
body: Repos live in the `repos` table and are connected through `POST /api/repos`; FACTORY_REPOS only seeds it at boot (control/config.py `_repos`, control/repos.py `seed`) and removing an entry never unwatches anything. `control/repos.py` holds an in-memory cache because `settings.repos` was read synchronously by the poller, the plan page, the projects page and preflight — every write goes through that module and reloads, so nothing may write `db.add_repo`/`remove_repo`/`set_repo_golden` directly. The poller starts unconditionally and re-reads `repos.watched()` each tick, so a repo connected at 10:00 is polled at 10:00:30 with no restart. Provisioning a warm golden is a run with `kind = 'provision'` (control/provision.py) and its `repos.provision_status` is a report, never a gate: an unprovisioned, failed or half-warmed repo still dispatches onto golden-copy and installs for itself. Never make connecting or dispatching wait on a snapshot.

title: telemetry/config.py's db_path is a plain module attribute, not a frozen settings object
body: Unlike control/config.py's `settings` (frozen, so tests use `object.__setattr__`), telemetry/config.py just exposes `db_path` as a bare module-level `Path`. A test pointing telemetry at a throwaway SQLite file assigns `config.db_path = ...` directly before calling `store.init()` — `store.connect()` re-reads `config.db_path` on every call rather than binding it at import, so the reassignment is picked up without any patching helper (control/repos_test.py's pattern is close but heavier than telemetry needs).

title: Memory receipts persist from _stream, scanning decoded JSON event text not raw wire lines
body: control/runner.py now wires the FACTORY_MEMORY receipt (mem_6a59) to telemetry: _stream watches every JSON stream-json event for a receipt and, on the first valid one, calls telemetry.store.write_memory_reads (one row per opened id) inside a try/except that only logs on failure (AC4) — a receipt never fails or stops the run. The receipt line is NOT a raw wire line like the FACTORY-MANIFEST prefix (which the shell script echoes outside the agent); the agent prints it as its own turn text or via a shell echo, so it only exists with real newlines after json.loads(line) decodes the assistant message content blocks (text and tool_result). Scanning the raw undecoded line (as parse_memory_receipt alone would if fed the wire text) misses it because `\n` is still two characters there. See runner._receipt_candidates. telemetry.store.memory_metrics_by_repo() (new) joins memory_reads to runs.repo, the same table unit_economics already reads, to avoid a second source of repo truth; usage_for_run() now also returns a `memory` key.

title: A supersession's NEW record goes in domains/ as active; only the OLD one moves to archive/
body: control/memory.py's `validate` command (run as `python -m control.memory validate .` in CI) fails the build if any id in index.jsonl has no matching status=active line in domains/. A prior run on #51 wrote the new record (mem_b0df, which supersedes mem_6a59) straight into archive/repository.jsonl with status=superseded, instead of domains/repository.jsonl with status=active -- leaving its index.jsonl line pointing at nothing. Per the memory skill's §6: append the NEW record to domains/<domain>.jsonl as active, and move only the OLD id's line(s) to archive/ as superseded. The archive is for retired ids only, never for the record that just became current.
resolution: Move the misplaced record from archive/ to domains/ and set status back to active; supersedes stays pointed at the old id.

title: Admission-control tables (e.g. memory_candidates) live in control/db.py as INSERT OR IGNORE plus an explicit transition-edge dict
body: For issue #52 (memory_candidates), the queue followed control/db.py's existing repos-table shape: idempotent insertion via `INSERT OR IGNORE` on the primary key (fields dict includes id, so a resubmission is silently dropped and the first insert's fields win), and status transitions gated by a plain `dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]` of allowed edges (e.g. {"pending": ("accepted", "rejected")}) rather than a state machine library. transition_candidate() raises ValueError on any disallowed edge (including repeating a terminal transition) rather than returning False, so callers can't mistake "no-op" for "just happened". Tests follow control/repos_test.py's shape: point settings.db_path at a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() via object.__setattr__ (settings is frozen), then asyncio.run(db.init()) once at module scope.

title: CI runs `python -m control.memory validate .` and fails hard if index.jsonl summaries drift from domain record titles
body: CI's third gate (after ruff and the *_test.py loop, neither of which the issue prompt mentions) runs `python -m control.memory validate .` and treats any mismatch between a .mem/index.jsonl entry's `title` and its full record's `title` in .mem/domains/*.jsonl as a hard failure, not a lint warning. This bit issue #52's first attempt: the PR was reviewed and approved, then CI failed post-merge-approval because the index summary line was written with slightly different wording than the domain record. Before pushing memory edits, run `.venv/bin/python -m control.memory validate .` yourself and confirm 'memory OK' — do not assume ruff+tests are the only gates just because they're the ones spelled out in the task prompt.

title: boxd's snapshots.create only queues the capture; reaping the machine aborts it
body: The SDK's `boxd.snapshots.create(machine_id, name)` returns once boxd has QUEUED the capture, not once it has been written. `control/provision.py` destroyed the machine in its `finally` immediately after, which aborts the capture permanently: the name is left in the fleet at `pending` with no version, `agents.available()` correctly refuses to dispatch onto it (restorable means `bool(version)`, never `status == 'ready'`), and the repos register meanwhile says the repo is warm. The live symptom was `golden-mithril-studio-software-factory v0 pending 0B` with no machine behind it while every run for that repo still booted `golden-copy`. `scripts/build-golden.sh` never hit it because the `boxd snapshots save` CLI blocks until the capture lands. Any code path that captures a snapshot must wait via `agents.wait_until_captured(boxd, name, was, timeout, poll)` before deleting the machine, and must compare against the version the name carried BEFORE the capture — a re-save publishes a new version under a name that already has one, so testing for mere existence returns instantly and reproduces the bug. A capture that never lands is deleted rather than left in the fleet. Stubs in tests must model the delay (`control/warm_golden_test.py` `Snapshots`): a stub that publishes the finished snapshot synchronously cannot express this bug, which is why the ordering assertion `snapshots.create before machines.delete` passed for as long as the bug was live.

title: An index line's files must be evidence.files + dirs, or the record is never retrieved
body: SKILL.md §3.2 defines an index line's `files` as the record's `evidence.files` plus `evidence.dirs`, merged. Priming (§4 step 3) matches a working set against the index and nothing else, so a path in the record but missing from its index line means the record is simply never retrieved for that path. Unlike `domain`/`type`/`title`, which are copied verbatim, `files` is derived — it goes stale the moment a record's evidence grows and the line does not. Five of this repo's fourteen index lines had drifted this way and the store still validated clean.
resolution: control/memory.py's _check_index_consistency now compares the index line's `files` against the record's evidence as a set, reporting both omitted and invented paths. Order is not compared. scripts/verify.sh runs it, so a drifted line fails CI.

title: An empty FACTORY_MEMORY receipt is persisted, and stays provisional until one opens a record
body: The empty receipt exists so 'primed, opened nothing' and 'never reached step 1' do not look the same downstream, so it is written to `memory_receipts` even with no reads to attribute. It is also held provisionally: the build prompt spells the empty receipt out as valid JSON for an agent to copy, so anything echoing the prompt back through the stream carries a parseable receipt, and stopping at the first match let that echo claim the run. `_better_receipt` keeps listening until a receipt opens a record; the run-level row REPLACEs and the per-record rows IGNORE, so an upgrade costs one extra write and no wrong row.

title: Memory candidates: build-only env var, collected before both reaps, id derived from run + content
body: A run proposes learnings by appending JSONL to $FACTORY_MEMORY_CANDIDATES, and control reads the file out of the VM before it is destroyed. Three things are not obvious. The variable is set on build runs only (dispatch_env's `kind`), because the review prompt never asks for the file and an env var naming a file nobody collects invites writing into a void — vm_script_test pins the build/review env difference, so adding one means editing that list. Collection is called twice, after _salvage_transcript and again in the finally before the fallback reap, with a `collected` flag: the ordinary path misses every run that died in the stream, and that run's VM is reaped in the finally. The candidate id is sha256(run_id + content), not agent-chosen, so INSERT OR IGNORE deduplicates a double collection instead of silently dropping a second distinct learning that reused an id.

title: Skill loads are already recorded as tool_calls rows; no skills receipt is needed
body: `telemetry/normalize.py` HINT_KEYS contains "skill", and none of the keys ahead of it (command, file_path, pattern) appear in the Skill tool's input — so every skill invocation already lands in `tool_calls` as (tool='Skill', detail=<skill name>). Querying "which skills did this repo's runs actually load" needs no new table, no new marker in the stream, and no new promise from the agent; it is a join from `tool_calls` to `runs`. `telemetry.store.skill_loads_by_repo` and the `skills` section of `telemetry/digest.py` are that query. Before building anything that asks the agent to report on its own tool use, check whether `_hint` already captures it. The runtime's name for the tool lives in `normalize.SKILL_TOOL` because no table may name a runtime (docs/architecture.md 3.2) — import it rather than writing the string.

title: A personal skill overrides a project one, so a repo skill reusing a global name never loads
body: Claude Code resolves same-named skills as enterprise > personal > project — personal beats project, the opposite of the usual most-specific-wins. A golden installs the shared agent-skills into ~/.claude/skills (scripts/build-golden.sh), so a skill added to a target repo's .claude/skills/ under a name that already exists globally is not overridden loudly: it is never loaded at all. The pull request merges, the file sits in the repo unread, and telemetry.store.skill_loads_by_repo then reports it as having zero loads — which the improvement loop reads as 'unused' and proposes deleting. No step in that chain looks like an error. Related: e337dea removed a vendored copy of the memory skill so that skill has one home; a global skill does not belong in a repo at all.
resolution: Before adding a skill to a repo's .claude/skills/, run `ls ~/.claude/skills` and pick a name that is not there. When a repo skill shows zero loads, check for a global skill of the same name before concluding it is unused: a shadowed skill needs renaming, not deleting. LEARN_PROMPT_TEMPLATE in control/runner.py instructs both checks.

title: repos_test pins the register's exact column list; a repos migration edits that check in the same change
body: control/repos_test.py asserts `sorted(repos.rows()[0])` against the register's full column list, so any `ALTER TABLE repos ADD COLUMN` migration fails it until the expected list grows too. This is deliberate — the check exists so a column nobody remembers adding cannot ride along silently — which means the test edit belongs in the same commit as the migration, not in a follow-up after CI goes red. Hit while adding the Sentry columns (sentry_project, sentry_dsn, sentry_wiring_issue): everything else passed, only the pinned list failed. Also the register write rule from mem_9e41 extends to new columns: setters live in control/db.py but every caller goes through a control/repos.py wrapper that reloads the cache (record_sentry, record_sentry_wiring follow record_golden's shape).
